# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source

You can create an Amazon S3 direct-query data source through either the AWS Management Console or the OpenSearch Service API. The AddDataSource API operation creates a new data source in a domain. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Prerequisites

Before you create a data source, an OpenSearch domain must exist in your AWS account, and it must be version 2.13 or later. You must also have one or more S3 buckets in your account, one of which is used to store query checkpoints.

AWS Glue tables are optional prerequisites. However, to query data on Amazon S3, you need tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. These tables must be created using OpenSearch Query Workbench, because existing Hive tables are not compatible.

If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After the tables are created, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources that restrict access to limited tables.

A manually created IAM role is also optional, because OpenSearch Service can automatically create a role with the required permissions. If you create the role manually, you must attach the required permissions to it.

## Requirements for a manually created role

A manually created role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source, and they must allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. The role must also have a trust policy that allows directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com to assume it. Broader permissions such as s3:* or AdministratorAccess encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. If you need to support S3 buckets in different accounts, add a condition with the appropriate account to the S3 policy.

## After you create the data source

In the console, choosing Configure opens the data source details screen, which displays an OpenSearch Dashboards URL.

If fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source> is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only, and it is recommended that you not adjust its access. If you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is also deleted, and access is removed for any other users who were mapped to that deleted role.

Because fine-grained access control is enabled after you create a data source, the glue_access mapping is required. Non-admin users must be mapped to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access to run direct queries. You can manually create a back-end glue_access role and map it to the IAM role.

Finally, note the following about read access: a user with read access to the request index for a data source can read all queries against that data source, and a user with read access to the result index can read the results for all queries against that data source.

# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source

You can create an Amazon S3 direct-query data source through the AWS Management Console or through the OpenSearch Service API. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Before you begin

- **An OpenSearch Service domain running version 2.13 or later.** A domain must exist in your AWS account before you create a data source. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/createupdatedomains.html
- **S3 bucket(s) containing the data to query.** One or more S3 buckets must exist in your AWS account before you create a data source. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html
- **An S3 bucket to store query checkpoints.** Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html
- **AWS Glue Data Catalog tables pointing to the S3 data (optional).** Create them with OpenSearch Query Workbench; the default database can be used initially. Steps are on this page, in the section on AWS Glue tables below.
- **A manually created IAM role with a required permissions policy and a trust policy (optional).** You need this only if you do not let OpenSearch Service create the role. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-custom.html
- **An IAM identity policy on the manually created role** granting least-privilege es, glue and s3 access (see the sample policy). Steps are on this page, in the section on the IAM role below.
- **A trust policy on the manually created role** allowing OpenSearch Service to assume it. Steps are on this page, in the section on the IAM role below.

## AWS Glue tables

AWS Glue tables are optional prerequisites for creating the data source. However, querying data on Amazon S3 requires tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. Because of that, the tables must be created using OpenSearch Query Workbench. Existing Hive tables are not compatible, so the tables cannot be both Hive tables and the Data Catalog tables that querying requires.

This is the first time an Amazon S3 data source is being set up, so you must create an admin data source to configure all AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. Only after the tables are created can you create new Amazon S3 data sources that restrict access to limited tables. The admin data source comes first, and the restricted data sources follow.

## The IAM role

A manually created IAM role is optional, because OpenSearch Service can automatically create a role with the required permissions. If you create a role manually, you must attach the required permissions to it. Attaching them means the role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source, and they must also allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role.

Use the sample policy for least-privilege access. Broader permissions such as s3:* or AdministratorAccess encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support S3 buckets in different accounts, add a condition with the appropriate account to the S3 policy.

The role must also have a trust policy allowing directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com to assume the role.

## Create the data source

Using the API, the AddDataSource operation creates a new data source in a domain. In the console, choosing Configure opens the data source details screen, which shows an OpenSearch Dashboards URL.

## Fine-grained access control and permissions

Fine-grained access control is enabled after you create a data source, which requires the glue_access mapping. Non-admin users must be mapped to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access to run direct queries, and this holds only when fine-grained access control is enabled. You can manually create a back-end glue_access role and map it to the IAM role.

A user with read access to the request index for a data source can read all queries against that data source. A user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source.

When fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source> is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. We recommend that you do not adjust the access of this role.

## Deleting a data source

When you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is also deleted. Access is removed for other users mapped to the deleted role.

# Creating an Amazon S3 Direct-Query Data Source

You can create an Amazon S3 direct-query data source through either the AWS Management Console or the OpenSearch Service API. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Prerequisites

Before creating a data source, an OpenSearch domain must exist in your AWS account, and it must be version 2.13 or later. You must also have one or more S3 buckets in your account, one of which is used to store query checkpoints.

AWS Glue tables are optional prerequisites. However, if you want to query data on Amazon S3, you need tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. These tables must be created using OpenSearch Query Workbench; existing Hive tables are not compatible. If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After the tables are created, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources that restrict access to a limited set of tables.

A manually created IAM role is also optional, because OpenSearch Service can automatically create a role with the required permissions. If you create the IAM role manually, you must attach the required permissions to it.

## Creating the data source

With the API, the AddDataSource operation creates a new data source in a domain. In the console, choosing Configure opens the data source details screen, which displays an OpenSearch Dashboards URL.

## Required permissions for a manually created role

A manually created role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source and must allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. The role must have a trust policy that allows directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com to assume it. Broader permissions such as s3:* or AdministratorAccess encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support S3 buckets in different accounts, add a condition with the appropriate account to the S3 policy.

## Fine-grained access control

Fine-grained access control is enabled after you create a data source, which requires the glue_access mapping. Non-admin users must be mapped to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access in order to run direct queries. You can manually create a back-end glue_access role and map it to the IAM role.

When fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source> is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. It is recommended that you not adjust the access of this role.

A user with read access to the request index for a data source can read all queries against that data source. Likewise, a user with read access to the result index can read the results for all queries against that data source.

## Deleting a data source

When the data source is deleted, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is also deleted. As a result, access is removed for any other users who were mapped to the deleted role.

# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source

## Before you begin

- **An OpenSearch domain** in your AWS account, running version 2.13 or later. Create it before you create the data source.
- **One or more S3 buckets** in your AWS account. One bucket stores query checkpoints.
- **AWS Glue tables** (optional). Querying data on Amazon S3 requires tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. Create them with OpenSearch Query Workbench.
- **An IAM role** (optional). You can create one manually, or OpenSearch Service can automatically create a role with the required permissions.
- **An IAM identity policy** with least-privilege permissions for `es`, `glue` and `s3`, attached to the manually created role. You need this only if you create the role yourself. The steps are in the IAM role section of this page.

## Creating the data source

You can create an Amazon S3 direct-query data source through the AWS Management Console or through the OpenSearch Service API. In the API, the `AddDataSource` operation creates a new data source in a domain. In the console, choosing **Configure** opens the data source details screen, which shows an OpenSearch Dashboards URL. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Glue tables and admin data source

Querying data on Amazon S3 requires tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. You must create these tables with OpenSearch Query Workbench. Existing Hive tables are not compatible, so they cannot serve as the tables this requirement calls for.

If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. This requirement applies only to a first-time setup. Create the admin data source and the tables before you create further data sources. Once the tables exist, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources that restrict access to a limited set of tables.

## The IAM role

A manually created IAM role is optional, because OpenSearch Service can create a role with the required permissions automatically. If you create the role yourself, you must attach the required permissions to it. Attaching them is enough to satisfy two requirements: the role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source, and they must allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role.

The required permissions come from an IAM identity policy with least-privilege permissions for `es`, `glue` and `s3`. Broader permissions such as `s3:*` or `AdministratorAccess` encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support S3 buckets in different accounts, add a condition with the appropriate account to the S3 policy.

The role must also have a trust policy that allows `directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com` to assume the role.

## Fine-grained access control

You enable fine-grained access control after creating a data source. Non-admin users must be mapped to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access to run direct queries, and this applies only once fine-grained access control is enabled. You can manually create a back-end `glue_access` role and map it to the IAM role. Because fine-grained access control is enabled after you create the data source, the `glue_access` mapping is required.

When fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named `AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source>` is created automatically for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. Don't adjust the access of this role.

Two read permissions are worth noting. A user with read access to the request index for a data source can read all queries against that data source. A user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source.

## Deleting a data source

When you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is also deleted. Access is then removed for any other users who were mapped to that role.
